title: On Damon's Relative Contact Equivalences vs A-Equivalence of Complex Analytic Map-Germs
content: A central and important part of the singularity theory is the classification of map-germs by using the natural A-equivalence (changes of coordinates in source and target of map do not change the differential geometric properties of the singularities of the map). A-equivalence also known as an A-symmetry. In general, the classification of map-germs by A-equivalence is often complicated. However, there is another equivalence called K-equivalence (or contact equivalence) which is extremely useful in singularity theory to study the properties of the map under A-equivalence. In this paper, we use versions of K-equivalence, denoted KV-equivalence (respectively, VK-equivalence) by using K-equivalence that preserve a variety in the target (respectively, the source) of map-germs. These equivalences are called Damon's relative contact equivalences. In fact, we will give some results between KV-equivalence and VK-equivalence and we will use these results to prove the equivalence of map-germs up to A-equivalence.
